policy_title: Triple farmer support for nature-friendly farming
stated: Almost triple support to farmers over the next 5-year parliament to support the transition to nature-friendly farming, conserve soil and the wider environment, and link farm payments to a reduction in pesticides and agro-chemicals.

source.quote: Elected Greens will: • Almost triple support to farmers over the next 5-year parliament to support the transition to nature-friendly farming. • Conserve and improve the health of the soil and the wider environment, which in turn would lead to cleaner rivers. • Link farm payments to a reduction in the use of pesticides and other agro-chemicals.

bearing_set.reason: The policy explicitly targets pesticide/agro-chemical reduction, soil conservation, and wider environmental improvement — direct, first-order effects on water quality, biodiversity, and agricultural emissions.
Almost tripling public payments to farmers directly determines farm-sector income levels and financial viability, making it a real verdict on whether farming provides a decent, secure livelihood.

Linking payments to reduced pesticide/agro-chemical use and nature-friendly practices could alter farm yields and production costs, with a plausible pass-through to food prices (an explicit O2 indicator), creating a contested but non-negligible cross-outcome spillover.

'Almost tripling' public farm-support payments over a parliament is a material increase in public expenditure; whether it is funded or absorbed by the existing budget directly bears on the sustainability of the debt path — the concrete O12 mechanism.

membership_note: Two clear bearings: O6 is the primary designed-for outcome; O12 captures the non-negligible fiscal footprint of a major spending scale-up. Effects on food prices (O2) and aggregate productivity (O13) are plausible but too diffuse and indirect to clear the non-negligible bar at economy-wide level.
